text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on February 13 in history.
1542 - Catherine Howard, fifth wife of King Henry VIII of England, was executed for adultery.
1571 - Benvenuto Cellini, Italian sculptor and writer, died; noted for his famous bronze "Perseus with the head of Medusa".
1668 - Under the Treaty of Lisbon, Spain recognised the independence of Portugal.
1689 - William of Orange and his wife Mary, daughter of the deposed James II, were declared joint sovereigns of Great Britain and Ireland.
1692 - John Campbell, at the head of an English force, led the Glencoe massacre against the Macdonalds in Scotland.
1728 - Cotton Mather, champion of Puritanism and member of the Mather family prominent in 17th century New England, died.
1793 - Britain, Prussia, Austria, Holland, Spain and Sardinia formed an alliance against France.
1849 - Lord Randolph Churchill, British Conservative politician and father of future prime minister Winston, born.
1858 - Sir Richard Burton and Captain John Speke became the first Europeans to discover Lake Tanganyika in East Africa.
1883 - Wilhelm Richard Wagner, German composer, died. His most famous works include "Der Ring des Nibelungen" (The Ring of the Nibelung), "Tristan und Isolde" and "Parsifal".
1920 - Switzerland was admitted to the League of Nations.
1945 - Budapest fell to the Russians after a 50-day siege in which 50,000 Germans were killed.
1945 - British and U.S. air force planes bombed Dresden over 14 hours, killing at least 35,000 people.
1958 - Georges-Henri Rouault, French expressionist painter, died. He had been apprenticed to a stained-glass designer and his subsequent work manifested glowing colours, outlined with black.
1974 - Nobel prize-winning author Alexander Solzhenitsyn was deported from the Soviet Union and deprived of Soviet citizenship.
1976 - French-born U.S. coloratura soprano Lily Pons died. She achieved huge success in Paris, London, South America and, especially, at the New York Metropolitan Opera House.
1979 - Jean Renoir, French film maker, died. His "Nana", "La Grande Illusion", "La Bete Humaine", "The Golden Couch" and "Le Dejeuner sur l'herbe" are masterpieces of cinema.
1983 - A fire in a cinema in Turin, Italy, killed 64 people.
1990 - Roaring crowds gave Nelson Mandela a hero's welcome when he returned to the black township of Soweto with a message of moderation and a pledge to end "the dark hell of apartheid."
1991 - Up to 400 civilians, mainly women and children, were feared dead after U.S. bombs or missiles smashed into a packed Baghdad air raid shelter.
1992 - Ford Motor Co reported its biggest ever loss of $2.3 billion.
1994 - Up to 150 illegal Burmese workers, many of them women and children, were feared dead after a ferry boat taking them home capsized off Thailand.
1994 - The ruling Malawi Congress Party elected former detainee Gwanda Chakuamba as President Kamuzu Banda's virtual successor, naming him deputy to the country's supreme ruler of 30 years.
